$comment: The declared shipping method the basket and the checkout price against. ONE standard method, flat rates only, never a rate table: the plan's Global Constraints forbid calculated carrier rates, and live carrier rates are explicitly out of scope. BOTH AMOUNTS ARE OPERATOR-SUPPLIED COMMERCIAL FACTS, 2026-08-10 — on the same footing as every value in catalogue.json, not placeholders and not waiting on anybody. EUR 7.00 to a delivery address in an EU MEMBER STATE ('europeanUnion'), EUR 12.00 to one anywhere else ('restOfWorld'). BOTH RATES ARE NET, on the same rule as the product price (the operator, 2026-08-18): Estonian VAT is added to delivery inside the EU and to nothing else, so EUR 7.00 is EUR 8.68 on an EU buyer's bill and EUR 12.00 is EUR 12.00 everywhere else. 'ratesWithTax' carries those grossed figures as DATA, on exactly the same footing as catalogue.json's 'amountWithTax', because the gross figure is never COMPUTED here or anywhere in storefront/src: Medusa returns it on a real cart as shipping_total, and backend/src/commerce/tax-model.ts is the one place a rate is written down. backend/tests/commerce-shipping-model.test.ts derives both entries from the declared rate and the declared VAT percentage, so neither is a literal nobody owns. The two tables differ only where VAT is due, which is why 'restOfWorld' is the same figure twice rather than an omission. 'Member state' is narrower than 'in the EU', and the difference is not cosmetic: the zone is selected from the delivery address's country through storefront/mock/countries.json, whose 'euMember' flag is exactly the 27 member states, so Aland, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Reunion and Mayotte are delivery addresses in the EU that are charged the higher rate. That is also why the country field is a selection and not free text, because a rate driven from typed text charges 'eesti' the non-EU rate. The live Medusa shipping options are seeded to these two figures by backend/src/commerce/shipping-model.ts, and backend/tests/commerce-shipping-model.test.ts holds this file's two rates AND countries.json's 27 'euMember' flags to that model in both directions, so the figure this file prices with and the figure Medusa charges cannot drift apart. The dispatch and delivery estimates are NOT here: they are read verbatim from content/legal/shipping.ts, which is where they already exist. 'parcelMachine' is the SECOND method, added by operator decision of 2026-08-26 for Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania ONLY: a free Omniva parcel machine method sold alongside 'method' rather than instead of it, in the service zone backend/src/commerce/shipping-model.ts names 'Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania'. Its 'name' is the ONE PLACE the display name is written: the storefront cannot import the backend's model, so it recognises the parcel machine option among the ones Medusa returns by comparing that display name, and backend/tests/commerce-shipping-model.test.ts holds this string to PARCEL_MACHINE_OPTION_NAME so the two sides cannot name it differently. 'rate' is 0 and carries no 'rateWithTax' twin, unlike 'method': there is no VAT on nothing, so a second, identical zero would be a figure that could silently stop matching the first rather than a fact worth stating twice — backend/tests/commerce-shipping-model.test.ts asserts the rate is exactly 0 rather than leaving that unchecked. 'countries' is PARCEL_MACHINE_COUNTRY_CODES, and storefront/src/lib/cart.ts validates its shape on import for the same reason assertPriceable validates 'method': a block the storefront trusts and nothing checks is how a malformed rate reaches a buyer's screen. 'phoneOptionalCountries', added 2026-08-27, is a CARRIER RULE, not an operator decision and not a region: it is the exact set of destinations for which OMX (Omniva's shipment-registration API) does NOT require a receiver phone number, because the buyer's email already satisfies the carrier there. It is EE, FI, LT and LV — FOUR countries, and deliberately NOT the same set as 'parcelMachine.countries': Finland is in this list and has no parcel machine offered, so the two sets cannot be collapsed into one 'Baltic' name, and neither is named after a region anywhere in this codebase. This is the SAME MECHANISM 'parcelMachine.name' already uses to cross the storefront/backend boundary: storefront/src/lib/cart.ts validates this array's shape on import (assertPhoneOptionalCountries) and storefront/src/lib/store-checkout.ts's phoneRequiredForCountry reads it to decide whether the checkout asks for a phone number at all; backend/src/commerce/shipping-model.ts declares the identical set as PHONE_OPTIONAL_COUNTRY_CODES, which a later task's OMX shipment builder (backend/src/modules/omniva/shipment.ts) refuses to register a shipment without a phone outside of, and backend/tests/commerce-shipping-model.test.ts holds this array and that constant to each other in both directions. Two copies of a carrier rule with nothing comparing them is exactly how the storefront would end up asking for a phone number the backend does not require, or the reverse.
